\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نہلانا} (nahlānā)}{نہلانا (nahlānā)}]{\ur{نہلانا} (nahlānā) — to bathe (someone)}

\label{lesson:UR-C482-nahlana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to press gently, then the Urdu for to warm a sore place.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نہلانا}}
\textbf{\ur{نہلانا}} — \emph{nahlānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bathe (someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ماں} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{نہلایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māṅ ne bachche ko nahlāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother bathed the baby.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کتے} \ur{کو} \ur{نہلایا}, \emph{us ne kutte ko nahlāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نہلانا}} (\emph{nahlānā}) is the causative of \textbf{\ur{نہانا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to bathe\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{snāti}, \textquotedblleft{}bathes\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13786).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nahlānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nahlānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māṅ ne bachche ko nahlāyā.} — The mother bathed the baby.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to press gently, then the Urdu for to warm a sore place, then say \emph{nahlānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{نہلانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To bathe (someone)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مونڈنا} (mūṅḍnā)}{مونڈنا (mūṅḍnā)}]{\ur{مونڈنا} (mūṅḍnā) — to shave the head}

\label{lesson:UR-C482-mundna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to warm a sore place, then the Urdu for to bathe (someone).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مونڈنا}}
\textbf{\ur{مونڈنا}} — \emph{mūṅḍnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to shave the head\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{نائی} \ur{نے} \ur{بچے} \ur{کا} \ur{سر} \ur{مونڈا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāī ne bachche kā sar mūṅḍā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{داڑھی} \ur{مونڈی}, \emph{us ne dāṛhī mūṅḍī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مونڈنا}} (\emph{mūṅḍnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{mū̃ḍnā} under Sanskrit \emph{muṇḍayati}, \textquotedblleft{}shaves\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10194).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شیو} (shev)}{شیو (shev)}]{\ur{شیو} (shev) — a shave}

\label{lesson:UR-C482-shev}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to bathe (someone), then the Urdu for to shave the head.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شیو}}
\textbf{\ur{شیو}} — \emph{shev} — \textquotedblleft{}a shave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ابو} \ur{روز} \ur{صبح} \ur{شیو} \ur{بناتے} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{abbū roz subah shev banāte haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Dad shaves every morning.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شیو}} (\emph{shev}) is borrowed from English \emph{shave}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shev}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{abbū roz subah shev banāte haiṅ.} — Dad shaves every morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to bathe (someone), then the Urdu for to shave the head, then say \emph{shev} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کٹوانا} (kaṭvānā)}{کٹوانا (kaṭvānā)}]{\ur{کٹوانا} (kaṭvānā) — to have (something) cut}

\label{lesson:UR-C482-katvana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to shave the head, then the Urdu for a shave.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کٹوانا}}
\textbf{\ur{کٹوانا}} — \emph{kaṭvānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to have (something) cut\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{نائی} \ur{سے} \ur{بال} \ur{کٹوائے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne nāī se bāl kaṭvāe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I had my hair cut at the barber's.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{ناخن} \ur{کٹوائے}, \emph{us ne nākhun kaṭvāe}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کٹوانا}} (\emph{kaṭvānā}) is built on \textbf{\ur{کاٹنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to cut\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{kártati}, \textquotedblleft{}cuts\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2854): the form for having someone else do the cutting.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to shave the head, then the Urdu for a shave, then say \emph{kaṭvānā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تراشنا} (tarāshnā)}{تراشنا (tarāshnā)}]{\ur{تراشنا} (tarāshnā) — to trim; to pare}

\label{lesson:UR-C482-tarashna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a shave, then the Urdu for to have (something) cut.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تراشنا}}
\textbf{\ur{تراشنا}} — \emph{tarāshnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to trim; to pare\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادا} \ur{نے} \ur{اپنی} \ur{داڑھی} \ur{تراشی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādā ne apnī dāṛhī tarāshī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather trimmed his beard.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مونچھ} \ur{تراشی}, \emph{us ne mūṅchh tarāshī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تراشنا}} (\emph{tarāshnā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{tarāsh}, \textquotedblleft{}cutting\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{tarāshīdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to shave, to carve\textquotedblright{}, made into an Urdu verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarāshnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarāshnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dādā ne apnī dāṛhī tarāshī.} — My grandfather trimmed his beard.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a shave, then the Urdu for to have (something) cut, then say \emph{tarāshnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
